source.title: Selective Neuron Amplification in Transformer Language Models
source.authors: Ryyan Akhtar; P. Pahwa; Monika Arora

record.tranche_reason: The study uses task-responsive neurons as targets for activation scaling and reports task-performance results, but it does not test whether neurons have one or a small number of understandable jobs.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results from its own neuron-amplification method, including task performance, cross-task effects, and neuron-selection overlap. These results do not measure neuron interpretability, explanation accuracy on held-out activations, or attribution-graph sufficiency, so they map to none of V1–V7. Values from prior work cited in the paper are not included.
record.test_reason: The study selects feed-forward neurons by differential activation and scales them to improve task performance in GPT-2, with a preliminary Pythia-160M result. It reports only its own method's task gains. It never audits how many neurons have one job, never scores neuron explanations, and builds no attribution graphs. The authors say what the neurons compute 'remains an open question.'
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that baseline confidence predicts SNA effectiveness better than task type does, and recommend applying SNA only in low-confidence (Zone 1) cases. They report that the zone pattern carries over to SST-2 classification, that cross-task interference follows network depth, and that Pythia results are preliminary. They explicitly leave open what the amplified neurons compute.
record.recipe_differences: This is a task-enhancement intervention, not an audit of neuron jobs or held-out explanation testing. It selects neurons by differential activation and scales their feed-forward outputs during inference.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with baseline-confidence zone, task, layer, neuron count, multiplier, and—in the poetry task—prompt. The paper says Zone 2 was not directly tested; SST-2 required a margin-based zone definition and much higher multipliers than generation.

fits_no_version.finding: Lower baseline confidence goes with larger gains from selective neuron amplification (Spearman ρ = −0.762 across 12 tasks).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this SNA procedure on GPT-2 Medium, low baseline confidence predicts larger amplification gains.

fits_no_version.finding: Amplification effects vary by task and layer; Layer 8 arithmetic amplification interferes with poetry, but not the reverse.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Task-selected FFN neurons are not modular: amplifying early-layer ones affects other tasks, asymmetrically.

fits_no_version.finding: On zero-shot SST-2, low-margin predictions improve with Layer 21 amplification and high-margin ones do not. Overlap between positive and negative sentiment neurons depends on the contrast used to select them.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For zero-shot SST-2, the intervention's effect depends on the confidence-margin zone and on how sentiment neurons are selected.

record.problems: Core experiments are described as being on GPT-2 Small and Medium, but the detailed parameter sweep specifies GPT-2 Medium and its 24 layers; the paper does not clearly reconcile that scope. The authors say Zone 2 was not directly tested, describe Pythia-160M as preliminary, and note that the SST-2 baseline was zero-shot and below fine-tuned classifiers. The study does not identify what its amplified neurons compute.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for every layer, neuron-count, multiplier, or individual task configuration: the text gives aggregate summaries for these rather than separate reported outcome values. The SST-2 figure's unreported individual plotted values were not extracted.

untested.parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or of the shares with one, two or unknown jobs.
No interpretability shares measured for any model family, dense or MoE, at any scale.
No vision models, no InceptionV1 cat/car neuron, and no test of superposition versus recursive generalization.
No interpretable-neuron share measured across architectures, regularization or tools.
No attribution graphs and no comparison with replacement models or reconstruction error.
No neuron explanations are written or checked against held-out firing.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The neuron-level claims in the paper, such as Layer 10 neurons responding to 'if/then', are asserted without any reported measure, so they cannot support V1 or V6. The study's scope is inconsistent: GPT-2 Small is named, but the sweep is described only for GPT-2 Medium.

versions.untested_parts: No audit of Qwen3-32B neuron poles or proportions of poles with one job, two jobs, or unknown jobs.
No measurement of interpretability shares across model families, dense versus MoE models, or trillion-parameter models.
No analysis of the InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization, or superposition.
No measurement of interpretable-neuron shares by architecture, regularization, or tool quality.
No attribution graphs or comparison of neuron-based explanations with replacement models or reconstruction error.
No test of explanations against activations or firing locations beyond the examples used to write them.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: GPT-2 Medium

conditions.value: positive and negative sentiment neurons selected by differential activation against neutral text

rows.measure: Overlap between selected positive- and negative-sentiment neurons
rows.note: The paper says this overlap made targeted amplification unusable.
rows.check: This is a neuron-selection diagnostic, not an outcome. The 53% overlap reflects the neutral-text contrast, not neuron polysemanticity, so it should not be read as bearing on V1.
